Established in the 8th century when the Frankish king Pepin the Short granted land to the pope, this Italian sovereign territory was ruled directly by the Church until Italian unification in 1870 — what was it?
Papal States: Italian state ruled by the pope (756–1870)
Inheriting his mother's Burgundian domains at just three years old, which Habsburg ruler became the first of his dynasty to be crowned king of Castile, in 1506?
Philip the Handsome: Habsburg ruler, King of Castile in 1506. Philip was the son of Maximilian I of Austria and Mary of Burgundy.
Founder of a Mumbai travelling theatre company in 1944, this actor became the patriarch of a Hindi-film dynasty spanning four generations — who is he?
Blinded in one eye by childhood smallpox, he fought his first battle at ten and went on to found the Sikh Empire, capturing Lahore and ruling as its first maharaja. Who was he?
This member of a famous political dynasty spent decades in environmental law before becoming a high-profile anti-vaccine activist—and in 2025 took a Cabinet role. Who?
Robert F. Kennedy Jr.: American politician (born 1954)
SPONGE: Political pressure group. Its founder and first President was reported to be named James "Sandy" McMenemon.
A philosopher who held a chair in comparative religion at Calcutta before entering public life, this scholar rose from Vice President to President of India in 1962 — who was he?
Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan: President of India from 1962 to 1967. Radhakrishnan's philosophy was grounded in Advaita Vedanta, reinterpreting this tradition for a contemporary understanding.

Spurned in childhood as an illegitimate son, this early-19th-century monarch transformed his kingdom's army into a formidable fighting force during his reign from 1816 to 1828 — who was this Southern African king?
Shaka: Zulu king from 1816 to 1828. King Shaka was born in the lunar month of uNtulikazi (July) in 1787, in Mthonjaneni, KwaZulu-Natal Province, South Africa.
Stepping up from hostess for her assassinated husband, this Sri Lankan politician became, in 1960, the first woman in the world elected prime minister — who was she?
Sirimavo Bandaranaike: Prime Minister of Sri Lanka (1916–2000)
A British barrister who twice held the post of Home Secretary in 2022, this MP for Fareham made headlines in January 2026 by defecting from the Conservatives to Reform UK — who is she?
The son of Odysseus and Penelope, this young man sailed to Pylos and Sparta seeking news of his father, then helped slay the suitors back home in Ithaca — who is he?
Telemachus: Mythological son of Odysseus. When Telemachus reached manhood, he visited Pylos and Sparta in search of his wandering father.
A Gulf War veteran radicalized by Waco and Ruby Ridge, he carried out the 1995 Oklahoma City bombing — the deadliest act of domestic terrorism in U.S. history. Who was he?
This nontrinitarian Christian movement rejects the traditional three-in-one God concept, instead viewing Jesus Christ as a supreme moral teacher subordinate to a singular Creator — what is it?
The illegitimate son of Mircea I of Wallachia, this nobleman was inducted into the Order of the Dragon in 1431 and twice ruled Wallachia as Voivode in the 1430s and 1440s — who is he?
Vlad II Dracul: Ruler of Wallachia (r. 1436–1442, 1443–1447)
This unofficial coalition of countries officially allied with the United States during the Cold War stood in opposition to the Soviet Union and the Warsaw Pact — what was this group called?
Western Bloc: Group of states aligned with the United States during the Cold War. The name "Western Bloc" emerged in response to and as the antithesis of its communist counterpart, the Eastern Bloc.
A member of the influential 'Eight Elders' in 1980s China, this revolutionary politician is also the father of the country's current top Communist Party leader — who was he?

Commanding seven 'treasure voyages' across Asia under two Ming emperors, this admiral was a Muslim-born eunuch who received a new surname from the Yongle Emperor — who commanded these historic fleets?
Zheng He: Chinese Admiral and diplomat (1371–1433/1435)
Who among these four was born earliest?
Zhuge Liang (born 181) is the earliest of the four. After helping found Shu Han, Zhuge Liang exercised near-total authority over both civil and military affairs.
Which of these people was born first?
Ma Jun (mechanical engineer) (born 200) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these four was born earliest?
Zhuge Liang (born 181) is the earliest of the four. After helping found Shu Han, Zhuge Liang exercised near-total authority over both civil and military affairs.
Which of these four is the oldest?
Lisp (programming language) (founded 1958) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these is an astronomer?
Jabir ibn Hayyan is an astronomer. The c. 215 treatises that survive today mainly deal with alchemy and chemistry, magic, and Shi'ite religious philosophy.
Which one below is best known as a mathematician?
What is the atomic number of Rhodium?
Rhodium is a chemical element; it has symbol Rh and atomic number 45.
What is the atomic number of Argon?
Argon is a chemical element; it has symbol Ar and atomic number 18.
In what year was Carlos Slim born?
Carlos Slim Helú (Spanish: [ˈkaɾlos esˈlin eˈlu, - esˈlim -]; born 28 January 1940) is a Mexican business oligarch, investor and philanthropist.
In what year was Antoine Lavoisier born?
Antoine Lavoisier: It is generally accepted that Lavoisier's great accomplishments in chemistry stem largely from his changing the science from a qualitative to a quantitative one.
In what year was Travis Kalanick born?
Travis Kalanick: Travis Cordell Kalanick (born August 6, 1976) is an American businessman best known as the co-founder and former chief executive officer (CEO) of Uber.
In what year did Zhuge Liang die?
Zhuge Liang: After helping found Shu Han, Zhuge Liang exercised near-total authority over both civil and military affairs.
In what year did Marie Curie die?
Marie Curie: Curie was born in Warsaw, Russian Empire, where she studied at the clandestine Flying University and began her practical scientific training.
In what year was LSD discovered?
LSD taken orally has an onset of action of 0.4 to 1.0 hours and a duration of 7 to 12 hours.
TeX: Donald Knuth. TeX is a popular means of typesetting complex mathematical formulae; it has been noted as one of the most sophisticated digital typographical systems.
Tupolev Tu-204: Kazan Aircraft Production Association. It was developed for Aeroflot as a replacement for the medium-range Tupolev Tu-154 trijet in the 1990s.
In which country is British Aerospace 146?
British Aerospace 146: United Kingdom. Production figures include the Avro RJ, an improved version from Avro International Aerospace, a subsidiary of BAE Systems.
Who is credited with discovering Fructose?
Fructose: Augustin-Pierre Dubrunfaut. Fructose, or fruit sugar, is a common monosaccharide, i.e. a simple sugar.
Who is credited with discovering LSD?
LSD: Albert Hofmann. LSD taken orally has an onset of action of 0.4 to 1.0 hours and a duration of 7 to 12 hours.
Who is credited with discovering Manganese?
Manganese: Johan Gottlieb Gahn. Manganese is a chemical element; it has the symbol Mn and atomic number 25.

This mosquito species, native to tropical Southeast Asia and marked with distinctive white bands on its legs and body, has spread worldwide via international trade and travel, becoming a significant public health concern — what species is it?

Aedes albopictus (synonym Stegomyia albopicta), from the mosquito (Culicidae) family, also known as the (Asian) tiger mosquito or forest mosquito, is a species of mosquito native to the tropical and subtropical areas of Southeast Asia.
This parasitic intestinal illness, caused by Entamoeba histolytica, can produce cysts that survive for weeks in soil or nearly an hour under fingernails — what is it called?
Amoebiasis is an infection of the intestines caused by a parasitic amoeba Entamoeba histolytica.

This superfamily of tailless Old World primates, native to sub-Saharan Africa and Southeast Asia and more closely related to Old World monkeys than New World ones, includes humans among its members — what's this group called?
Ape (hominoids), are a superfamily of Old World simians native to sub-Saharan Africa and Southeast Asia.
These large Old World monkeys come in six distinct species, each native to a different region of Africa, with one species also found on the Arabian Peninsula — what primate is it?
Baboon are primates comprising the genus Papio, one of the 23 genera of Old World monkeys, in the family Cercopithecidae.
From molecules and cells up to whole ecosystems, this science studies living things through ideas like heredity, evolution, and homeostasis — what is it?
Biology is the scientific study of life and living organisms.
Present in both sexes from the same embryonic tissue, these two prominences on the upper torso permanently enlarge only in human females at puberty, driven by estrogen and growth hormone - name them?
Breast are two prominences located on the upper ventral region of the torso in humans and other primates.
Discovered in 1940, this non-intoxicating compound extracted from cannabis is used medically as an anticonvulsant for two rare, severe forms of childhood epilepsy — what is it?
Cannabidiol (CBD) is a phytocannabinoid, one of 113 identified cannabinoids in Cannabis, along with tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), and accounts for up to 40% of the plant's extract.
First cultivated in Mesoamerica and later spread worldwide during the Columbian Exchange, this edible gourd-family plant is also known as christophine, mirliton, or choko — what is it?

Chayote (previously placed in the obsolete genus Sechium, now in the genus Sicyos, as Sicyos edulis), also known as christophine, mirliton, gisquil, and choko, is an edible plant belonging to the gourd family, Cucurbitaceae.
Its glorious blue in glass and paint was long wrongly blamed on bismuth, and frustrated miners named its ore after a goblin. Which hard, gray element carries the symbol Co?
Cobalt is a chemical element; it has symbol Co and atomic number 27.
Which vanilla-scented, benzopyrone lactone compound acts as a plant's chemical defense against predators and, via its derivatives, gave rise to the anticoagulant warfarin?
Coumarin is an aromatic organic chemical compound with formula C9H6O2.
The word names both a noun — a plan or proposal made by a thinking agent — and a verb for developing one, always aiming to satisfy goals while weighing function and aesthetics; what is it?
Design is the concept or proposal for an object, process, or system.
Partly blinded in a childhood fishing accident, this Alabama-born naturalist turned to insects, co-developed the theory of island biogeography, and founded the field of sociobiology. Who is he?
E. O. Wilson (June 10, 1929 - December 26, 2021) was an American biologist, naturalist, ecologist, and entomologist who developed the field of sociobiology.
Also known as human herpesvirus 4, this common virus was the first identified oncogenic virus and causes infectious mononucleosis in 90% of cases. What is it?
Epstein–Barr virus (EBV), also known as human herpesvirus 4 (HHV-4), is one of the nine known human herpesvirus types in the herpes family, and is one of the most common viruses in humans.
Which group of vascular plants, which reproduce via spores rather than seeds or flowers, are known for their large megaphyll leaves and the coiled 'fiddleheads' many species unfurl as new growth?
Fern (Polypodiopsida or Polypodiophyta) are a group of vascular plants (land plants with vascular tissues such as xylem and phloem) that reproduce via spores and have neither seeds nor flowers.

Lasting anywhere from milliseconds to hours, these are the most luminous explosions in the universe after the Big Bang, sometimes triggered when massive stars collapse into black holes — what are they?
Gamma-ray burst (GRBs) are extremely energetic events occurring in distant galaxies that represent the brightest and most powerful class of explosion in the Universe.
Comprising about 50 species native to tropical regions worldwide, this genus produces roughly 80% of the world's natural fiber and doubles as an oilseed crop — which genus?
Gossypium is a genus of flowering plants in the tribe Gossypieae of the mallow family, Malvaceae, from which cotton is harvested.
In their healthy state these vascular cushions in the anal canal actually help with stool control — it's only when they swell or inflame that they earn the nickname "piles." What are they?
Hemorrhoid (or haemorrhoids), also known as piles, are vascular structures in the anal canal.
This negatively charged ion, one oxygen bonded to one hydrogen, acts as a base and forms industrially vital salts like the sodium version used to make millions of tons of chemicals. What ion is it?
Hydroxide (occasionally hydroxyl ion) is a diatomic anion with chemical formula OH.

Acting as the eye's diaphragm in optical terms, this thin ring-shaped structure controls how much light reaches the retina by adjusting the pupil's size, and also determines a person's eye color — name this structure?

Iris (anatomy) (pl.: irides or irises) is a thin, ring-shaped structure in the eye in most mammals and birds that is responsible for controlling the diameter and size of the pupil, and thus the amount of light reaching the retina.
England's very first Astronomer Royal, he compiled a 3,000-star catalogue and even spotted Uranus — though he mistakenly logged it as a star. Who was he?
John Flamsteed (19 August 1646 - 31 December 1719) was an English astronomer and the first Astronomer Royal.
Despite being a kingfisher, this Australian bird rarely goes near water and can grow up to about 47 centimeters long — what is it?
Kookaburra are terrestrial tree kingfishers of the genus Dacelo native to Australia and New Guinea, which grow to between 28 and 47 cm (11 and 19 in) in length and weigh around 300 g (11 oz).
This genus of large-flowered bulb plants is prized in gardens worldwide but is highly toxic to cats. What genus is it?
Lilium is a genus of herbaceous flowering plants growing from bulbs, all with large and often prominent flowers.
Members of the family Scombridae, these open-ocean fish sport forked tails and green-blue tiger stripes, often wintering in deep water after a coastal spawning run — what fish are they?
Mackerel is a common name applied to a number of different species of pelagic fish, mostly from the family Scombridae.
This cone-shaped structure at the base of the brainstem controls involuntary functions from heart rate and breathing to vomiting and sneezing — what is it called?
Medulla oblongata is a long stem-like structure which makes up the lower part of the brainstem.

Attaching to its host tree through a structure called the haustorium to steal water and nutrients, this hemiparasitic plant has one species native to the British Isles and much of Europe — what is it?
Mistletoe is the common name for obligate hemiparasitic plants in the order Santalales.
Known for strong anabolic but weak androgenic effects, this synthetic androgen is marketed as Deca-Durabolin and used to treat muscle-wasting and bone-density conditions — which steroid?
Nandrolone is an endogenous androgen. Nandrolone esters are used in the treatment of anemias, cachexia (muscle wasting syndrome), osteoporosis, breast cancer, and for other indications.
What organic molecule, composed of a nitrogenous base, a five-carbon sugar, and a phosphate group, serves as the basic building block of both DNA and RNA?
Nucleotide are organic molecules composed of a nitrogenous base, a pentose sugar and a phosphate.
This rare silvery-white metal, discovered in 1802 and named after a newly found asteroid, is part of the six-element platinum group and has the lowest melting point among them. What element is it?
Palladium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Pd and atomic number 46.

Nicknamed with the backronym 'Practical Extraction and Reporting Language,' this dynamic scripting language was developed by Larry Wall in 1987 and borrows features from C, AWK, and sed — which language?
Perl is a high-level, general-purpose, interpreted, dynamic programming language.
Caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis and often spread by flea bites, this disease comes in pneumonic, bubonic, and septicemic forms — what is it?
Plague (disease) is an infectious disease caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis. There are three forms of plague, each affecting a different part of the body and causing associated symptoms.
Including raccoons, coatis, kinkajous, and ringtails, this New World mammal family within the order Carnivora is made up mostly of omnivores — what family is it?
Procyonidae is a New World family of the order Carnivora. Procyonidae ( PROH-see-ON-i-dee) is a New World family of the order Carnivora.
Decades after leaving the Communist Party of Spain to found the United Left, which economist re-emerged in 2023 as an unlikely no-confidence-vote candidate?
Ramón Tamames (born 1 November 1933) is a Spanish economist and former politician.
This woody perennial flowering plant, genus Rosa in the family Rosaceae, includes over 300 species and tens of thousands of cultivars, with sharp prickles on many stems — name the flower?
Rose is either a woody perennial flowering plant of the genus Rosa, in the family Rosaceae, or the flower it bears.
About 950 species of these spiny, globe-shaped marine animals crawl the seabed on tube feet, found from tide pools down to 5,000 metres deep. What are they?
Sea urchin are the class Echinoidea within the echinoderms.

Named from an Ancient Greek word for 'soap,' this cheesy secretion of shed skin cells, oils, and moisture collects under the foreskin in males and around the folds of female genitalia — what is it called?
Smegma (from Ancient Greek, smgma, 'soap') is a cheesy substance composed of shed skin cells, skin oils, and moisture that occurs in male and female mammalian genitalia.
Known by his online username 'spez,' this web developer co-founded an airfare search engine before leading the world's seventh most-visited website as CEO — who is he?
Steve Huffman (born 1983 or 1984), also known by his Reddit username spez, is an American web developer and entrepreneur.
One of the oldest constellations, this zodiac figure once marked the Sun's place at the spring equinox and inspired bull imagery from Sumer to Rome — which northern-sky constellation is it?
Taurus (constellation) (Latin, 'Bull') is one of the constellations of the zodiac and is located in the northern celestial hemisphere.
Found in nature only as an oxide and locked in minerals like rutile and ilmenite, this strong, silvery element bears the name of mythological giants — what is it?
Titanium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ti and atomic number 22.
A physician before politics, this German served as Angela Merkel's defence minister and in 2019 became President of the European Commission — who is she?
Ursula von der Leyen (ne Albrecht; born 8 October 1958) is a German politician and physician who has served as President of the European Commission since 2019.
This small insect-eating songbird breeds across most of Europe and Asia, migrates to Africa in winter, and has a black-backed form that predominates in Britain and Ireland — what is it?
White wagtail (Motacilla alba) is a small passerine bird in the family Motacillidae, which also includes pipits and longclaws.
The only living member of its entire mammalian order, this nocturnal African burrower uses its long snout and powerful claws to dig ants and termites out of their mounds — what animal is it?
Aardvark: Burrowing mammal native to Africa.
While bacteria and some plants may be biologically immortal, this universal process in humans slows reaction time even as knowledge tends to grow — what is it called?
Ageing: Biological process of getting older.
Though commonly called a nut, this tree's fruit is technically a drupe with a hard shell surrounding an edible seed, closely related to the peach — which food is it?
Almond: Species of nut. The fruit of the almond is a drupe, consisting of an outer hull and a hard shell with the seed, which is not a true nut.
This Manchester physicist shared the 2010 Nobel Prize for his work on graphene — and is the only person to also hold an Ig Nobel, won for levitating a frog with magnetism. Who is he?
Also known as Umbelliferae and including carrots, celery, parsley, and dill, this plant family also contains dangerously toxic members like poison hemlock and giant hogweed — which family?
Originally conceived as the average Earth-Sun distance before its 2012 redefinition, this measure equals about 499 light-seconds and underpins the definition of the parsec — what is it called?
Astronomical unit: Mean distance between Earth and the Sun.

Baruch Goldstein: American-Israeli mass murderer (1956–1994). Goldstein was a supporter of Kach, a religious Zionist party that the United States, the European Union and other countries designate as a terrorist organization.
This natural science rests on five big themes — the cell, genes and heredity, evolution, energy transformation, and homeostasis — to explain life itself. What field is it?

Bred in South Africa as a family guard dog, this large mastiff-type breed has a short coat and heavy bone structure, and is recognized by that country's kennel union but not the international federation — what breed is it?
Boerboel: South African breed of dog. The Boerboel (pronounced [ˈbuːrbul]) is a South African breed of large dog of mastiff type, used as a family guard dog.
An intact, more muscular and aggressive adult male of the cattle species, this animal has long been a sacrificial symbol in many religions and stars in famous arena sports. What is it?
Bull: Adult male cattle. A bull is an intact (i.e., not castrated) adult male of the species Bos taurus (cattle).
Also known as hemp when grown for fiber rather than its psychoactive use, this Asian-native plant genus includes up to three disputed species — which plant?
Also known as an Ovcharka, this large livestock-guardian breed was developed in the Soviet Union around 1920 from mountain and steppe animals of the Caucasus region — which breed?
Caucasian Shepherd Dog: Russian breed of livestock guardian dog. It was bred in the Soviet Union from about 1920 from dogs of the Caucasus Mountains and the steppe regions of Southern Russia.
Covered in coarse black hair but bare-faced, this great ape is humans' closest living relative according to fossil and DNA evidence, and lives in groups of up to 150 — which species?
Chimpanzee: Species of great ape. The chimpanzee (Pan troglodytes), also simply known as the chimp, is a medium-sized great ape species found in the forests and savannas of equatorial Africa.
Sold as Catapres and Kapvay, this drug treats high blood pressure, ADHD, and drug-withdrawal symptoms, and can be delivered via a skin patch — what is it?
Renowned for a gift of mimicry noted by Pliny the Elder and Shakespeare, this glossy black bird has a bill that turns from black in winter to yellow in summer — what species is it?
Common starling: Species of passerine birds.

This academic framework examines how systemic bias against certain ethnic groups is embedded in laws and institutions, using the concept of intersectionality to explain overlapping forms of inequality — what is it called?
Critical race theory: Conceptual framework. The word critical in the name is an academic reference to critical theory, not criticizing or blaming individuals.

Dubbed the 'father of modern experimental optics,' this Scottish inventor discovered the angle and the photoelasticity that bear on polarized light — and improved the stereoscope along the way. Who was he?
David Brewster: British astronomer and mathematician (1781–1868)
Sold as Benadryl, this first-generation H1-antihistamine is famously sedating — yet at higher doses it can paradoxically cause agitation and restlessness instead of sleep; what's the drug?
Diphenhydramine: Antihistamine medication. Diphenhydramine, sold under the brand name Benadryl among others, is an antihistamine and sedative.
Named for its 'skin wings,' this insect order sports pincer-like cerci on its abdomen and displays unusually attentive maternal care for its young — which insect?
Earwig: Order of insects. Damage to foliage, flowers, and various crops is commonly blamed on earwigs, especially the common earwig Forficula auricularia.

This discipline systematically applies science and math to design solutions like bridges, pacemakers, and spacecraft, with traditional branches in civil, mechanical, electrical, and chemical work — which field?
This small finch native to Europe and Asia is the original species to bear its common English name, and goes by 'plum bird' in Shropshire — what is it?
Eurasian bullfinch: Species of bird. The Eurasian bullfinch or common bullfinch (Pyrrhula pyrrhula) is a small passerine bird in the finch family, Fringillidae.

Colloquially called squirting or gushing, this fluid is expelled from the Skene's gland near the urethra around the time of orgasm — and researchers stress it's physiologically distinct from coital incontinence. What is it?
Female ejaculation: Expulsion of fluid during orgasm.
This double-layered fold of skin covering the glans is attached by an elastic band called the frenulum and is typically fused in place at birth — what is it?
Foreskin: Retractable fold of skin which covers and protects the glans of the penis.
Often triggered by H. pylori infection or NSAID use, this inflammation of the stomach lining can, in its autoimmune form, lead to pernicious anemia — what condition is it?
Gastritis: Inflammation of the stomach lining. It may occur as a short episode or have a long duration.

Making up about 15% of all brain tumors and thought to arise from cells called astrocytes, this aggressive cancer often announces itself only with vague headaches or sudden personality changes — what is it?
Glioblastoma: Aggressive type of brain cancer. Initial signs and symptoms of glioblastoma are nonspecific.

Native to the Amazon basin, this climbing plant's coffee-bean-sized seeds can be up to 6% caffeine — double a green coffee bean — making it a staple in Brazilian soft drinks and energy drinks — which plant?
Also known as the Burgundy snail and served as escargot, this large air-breathing land snail native to Europe has a globular brown shell — what species is it?
German anthropologist Otto Schoetensack named this archaic human species in 1908 based on a jawbone found near the village of Mauer — then Europe's oldest known human fossil. Which species?

Homo heidelbergensis: Extinct species of archaic human. H. heidelbergensis has been regarded as either the last common ancestor of modern humans, Neanderthals, and Denisovans; or as a completely separate lineage.
Formed when chlorine dissolves in water, this compound is the main disinfecting agent in chlorine solutions — and your own white blood cells make it to fight off invading germs. What is it?
Hypochlorous acid: Chemical compound. Hypochlorous acid is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula ClOH, also written as HClO, HOCl, or ClHO.

This neurological emergency is sudden bleeding directly into brain tissue or its fluid-filled cavities — not from a blocked vessel, but a burst one — causing anything from headache to sudden paralysis. What is it?
Intracerebral hemorrhage: Type of intracranial bleeding that occurs within the brain tissue itself.
He won the Fields Medal in 1954 and, nearly half a century later, the very first Abel Prize in 2003 — which French mathematician of algebraic topology and geometry is it?

Conceived as a high-speed 'Schnellbomber' for the German Luftwaffe, this twin-engined WWII aircraft evolved into everything from a night fighter to the explosive lower half of composite 'Mistel' combinations — what is it?
Junkers Ju 88: German twin-engined multirole combat aircraft.

Nicknamed 'acid' and 'Lucy' and derived from the ergot fungus, this semisynthetic hallucinogen is so potent that 20 micrograms produces noticeable effects — yet no fatal human overdose has ever been documented — what is it?
Born in Germany, this businessman founded the first company to manufacture blue jeans, beginning operations in San Francisco in 1853 — who is he?
Marketed as Imodium, this opioid-class medication treats diarrhea without crossing the blood-brain barrier at normal doses?
Loperamide: Medicine used to reduce diarrhea.
Males of this widespread dabbling duck species sport iridescent green heads, while females have brown-speckled plumage — which bird?
Mallard: Species of duck. The mallard or wild duck (Anas platyrhynchos) is a dabbling duck that breeds throughout the temperate and subtropical Americas, Eurasia, and North Africa.
Distinguished by its darker camouflage, conformal fuel tanks, and a two-seat cockpit, this all-weather multirole fighter first flew in 1986 for long-range interdiction missions — what is it?
McDonnell Douglas F-15E Strike Eagle: American all-weather multirole fighter aircraft.
First made in 1969 and approved for medical use in 1978, this selective beta blocker treats high blood pressure, angina, and helps prevent migraines — what is it called?
Metoprolol: Beta blocker medication. It is also used to prevent further heart problems after myocardial infarction and to prevent headaches in those with migraines.
Sold under the brand name Provigil, this first-line narcolepsy treatment boosts dopamine without the euphoria or addiction risk of classic stimulants like amphetamine — what is it?
Lacking a cell wall entirely, this genus of bacteria is naturally resistant to beta-lactam antibiotics that target cell-wall synthesis — which genus?
Mycoplasma: Genus of bacteria. Mycoplasma is a genus of bacteria that, like the other members of the class Mollicutes, lack a cell wall (peptidoglycan) around their cell membrane.

Published in the Principia Mathematica, this principle holds that every particle in the cosmos attracts every other with a pull proportional to their masses and inversely proportional to the squared distance between them — which principle is it?
Newton's law of universal gravitation: Classical statement of gravity as force.
This medical condition, defined by a body mass index over 30, is linked to heart disease, type 2 diabetes and sleep apnea — what is it?
Obesity: Medical condition of excess body fat.
This fluid-filled sac that forms within the ovary is usually harmless and often tied to ovulation, appearing as a follicular or corpus luteum type — what is it?
Ovarian cyst: Fluid-filled sac in the ovary. If the cyst either breaks open or causes twisting of the ovary, it may cause severe pain.

He co-founded Microsoft with his childhood friend Bill Gates in 1975, then stepped back from daily work in 1983 after a Hodgkin lymphoma diagnosis and later launched Vulcan Inc. with his sister. Who was he?
Named from the Greek word for 'apparition' due to their leaf-like camouflage, this insect order includes stick insects and leaf insects. What's it called?
Phasmatodea: Order of stick and leaf insects.
Named from a Greek word meaning 'wanderers,' these large rounded bodies orbit a star or similar object — our solar system has eight, from Mercury to Neptune. What are they called?
Planet: Large, round non-stellar astronomical object.
Marked by high blood pressure and protein in the urine after 20 weeks of pregnancy, this disorder can progress to seizures if left untreated — what is it called?
This seabird's large, colorful beak fades after breeding season, and its short wings beat up to 400 times a minute to keep it airborne — what bird is it?

In a late stage of stellar evolution, this puffed-up, low-to-intermediate-mass star has a surface temperature around 5,000 K and burns helium or hydrogen in shells around its core — what type of star is it?
Red giant: Type of large cool star.
Also called a dassie, this small African and Middle Eastern mammal lives in crevice colonies of up to 80 and posts lookouts to warn of approaching predators — which animal?
Rock hyrax: Species of mammal native to Africa and the Middle East.
Dropped out of Stanford to co-found Loopt, later led Y Combinator, then became CEO of the company behind ChatGPT — briefly ousted by its board in 2023 for not being 'consistently candid.' Who is he?
Sam Altman: American entrepreneur and investor (born 1985)
Encompassing several superfamilies and families, this taxonomic order groups together cephalopods that each have ten arms — which order is it?
These slow-moving South American mammals hang upside down in rainforest canopies, are kin to anteaters, and — despite the "two-toed" label — all have three toes on each rear limb; what are they?
Sloth: Group of tree dwelling mammals noted for slowness.
Native to China and Vietnam but now invasive across the US after spreading through South Korea and Japan, this planthopper prefers the also-invasive tree of heaven as its host — what insect is it?
Spotted lanternfly: Species of planthopper indigenous to Southeast Asia.
